newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government is considering cancelling about five billion rand in spending from its huge rollovers from previous fiscal years as a means of keeping a lid on the deficit, a source said.

- The slide in the gold price in recent weeks could out pressure on the African Mining Consortium which bought 34.9 pecent of JCI from Anglo American Corp in November, as it seeks to fund the 2.8 billion rand deal, industry sources said.
- Would-be visitors to former jail Robben Island have been queuing at Cape Town's harbour from 4 a.m. to get tickets for the trips.
- The South African Police Service and Imperial Fleet Services have launched a two year scheme to improve management and maintenance of the police force's 32,000 vehicles.
- Two members of parliament, Marcel Golding and John Copelyn, are set to leave politics to become directors at Hosken Consolidated Investments.
- Gold's precipitous decline continued as it slipped below the psychologically crucial $360 an ounce level to fix in London at $358.50.
- Wage negotiations are expected to be tougher this year because of the anticipated increase in the inflation rate, according to labour consultancy Andrew Levy & Associates.
- South Africa's economic downturn is sharper than perceived, judging from the significant rise in dishonoured cheques.

- Right-winger Jan de Wet, wanted in connection with Christmas Eve bombings in Worcester, was arrested on a West Rand smallholding belonging to a "general" of the right-wing Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB).
- The family of Stephen Pon, a doctor killed by hijackers near Johannesburg Hospital last year, have had to come to terms with another tragedy -- the brutal slaying of a close relative.

- The South African soccer squad's preparation for the World Cup qualifier against Zambia in Lusaka on Saturday received a major boost with the arrival of foreign-based stars Lucas Radebe and Philemon Masinga.
